protocol.description:
Shared evaluation protocol: windows, ground truth, cohorts, candidate pools, popularity fill.

  validation: train on ISO weeks 11-20, ground truth from weeks 21-30
  final:      train on weeks 11-30, predict weeks 31-42
  truth:      a user's top-5 programmes by number of watched airings in the target weeks
              (ties: larger summed overlap_s of those watched airings, then smaller numeric id)
  cohort A:   submission users with >= 5 programmes in the truth
  cohort C:   all log users with >= 5 (sampled down to 20,000 with seed 42 if larger)
  pool:       tv_show_id != 0 airing in the target window's ISO weeks; repeats of watched programmes allowed
  fill:       cold-start users and lists shorter than 5 are topped up from popularity -> exactly 5 distinct ids

off_grid.note: off-grid, not used for selection (вне сетки, для выбора не использовались)

counts_f64_reg0.01_a1.note: off-grid, not used for selection (вне сетки, для выбора не использовались)

hyperparameters.definition: Content-based filtering on programme metadata, on the shared protocol; then a

columns.repeats_A: share of slots watched by the user in train
columns.mean_popularity_A: mean distinct train users per recommended programme (of 4737)

runtime_s.ppr: PageRank iterations + ranking for 4,030 users; graph build is shared and listed once
runtime_s.hybrid: PPR graph build + ranking + MF fit/ranking (depth 50) + fusion

ppr.rule: one variable per experiment; selection on MAP@5 A; replace baseline only if strictly better

robustness.note: post-hoc check, not used for selection; C minus A = cohort C users not in A; paired bootstrap of per-user AP@5 difference on A vs current PPR, 2000 resamples, seed 42

ppr_v3.definition:
Expected-frequency re-ranking of PPR v2 candidates, validation only (compared with v2).

  candidates   top-DEPTH programmes of PPR v2 (alpha, beta, H from results_validation.json["improve"])
  rate_ui      watched_ui / n_airings_train_i: watched_ui = sum of recency weights 0.5 ** (delta / H) of the
               user's watched airings (same H as v2); n_airings_train_i = plain count of labelled airings
               of the programme in the train window (items.parquet)
  expected_ui  rate_ui * n_airings_target_i (labelled airings in the target window, schedule only)
  score        expected_ui + lambda * ppr_ui / max_u(ppr), sorted descending; remaining ties keep PPR order
  check        "ppr_only" (expected switched off) must reproduce v2 exactly

hyperparameters.ppr_normalisation: score / max score among the user's candidates
hyperparameters.rate_denominator: plain count of train-window airings (not recency-weighted)

v2_signal.definition:
What counts as a training signal for PPR v2, validation only (compared with v2).

Only the training interactions fed to PPR (graph and restart) change; alpha, beta, H, the truth
(screen_time >= 0.8 in weeks 21-30), the pools and the popularity top-up stay as in the protocol.

  threshold T   a (user, airing) pair is a training interaction when screen_time >= T, weight 1 (x recency);
                T = 0.8 is v2
  soft T_min    pairs with screen_time >= T_min, weight = screen_time (x recency)
v2_signal.rule: accept only if MAP@5 A > v2 and the 95% CI of the A gain excludes 0
v2_signal.v5_rule: rebuild only if the best variant differs from the current v5, beats it on MAP@5 A and the 95% CI of the A gain over v5 excludes 0

v5_plus_slots.definition:
Channel x time-slot habits on top of v5, validation only (compared with v5).

  slot         (channel_id, day of week x hour of the airing start) -> key = channel_id * 168 + dow * 24 + hour
  profile      p_u(slot) = sum_weeks w_week * max signal of u in that slot and week / sum_weeks w_week over
               every ISO week of the train window (also weeks without viewing); signal and weights as in v5:
               screen_time of pairs with screen_time >= T_MIN, w_week = 0.5 ** ((end_week - week) / H).
               p_u is in [0, 1]: a recency-weighted share of weeks in which u watched that channel at that hour.
  slot_ui      sum over labelled airings of programme i in the target window (schedule only: which programme
               airs on which channel when) of p_u(slot of the airing) = expected number of airings watched
  ranking      candidates = v5 top-50 followed by slot-only programmes of the slot top-50;
               score = slot / max_u(slot) + lambda * v5 / max_u(v5); lambda = inf -> v5 only;
               zero scores dropped, ties keep candidate order, popularity top-up
  slot_only    pure slot_ui ranking (ties: smaller id), reported separately
v5_plus_slots.rule: accept only if MAP@5 A > v5 and the 95% CI of the A gain over v5 excludes 0
v5_plus_slots.v6_rule: rebuild only if the best lambda changed and the 95% CI of its gain over v5 excludes 0

lgbm_v6.definition:
Learned re-ranking on top of v6 with LightGBM lambdarank (validation + optional final).

Candidates per user: v6 top-50, then slot_ui top-50, then the user's pool programmes from the train window
(ordered by soft frequency), at most MAX_CANDIDATES. Every window-length dependent feature is per week
(train window: 10 weeks on validation, 20 on test; target window: 10 and 12 weeks).
History = train pairs with screen_time >= T_MIN (v5 signal); "hard" = screen_time >= 0.8.
Label = 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 for truth places 1-5, else 0.
Evaluation: features weeks 11-20, labels weeks 21-30, two folds of cohort-C users (seed 42), out-of-fold.
lgbm_v6.rule: accept only if OOF MAP@5 A > v6 and the 95% CI of the A gain over v6 excludes 0

final_v7.trained_on: 4030 cohort-C users, features weeks 11-20, labels weeks 21-30

feature_drift_submission_users.note: same 1,260 submission users; val window = weeks 11-20 -> 21-30, test window = weeks 11-30 -> 31-42; no labels exist for the test window

v7_refinement.definition:
Last refinement of the v7 re-ranker, same protocol (out-of-fold over two folds of cohort-C users).

  exp 1  label: binary (1 = programme in the truth) vs graded 5..1 (v7)
  exp 2  averaging: 5 models with subsample 0.8, subsample_freq 1, colsample_bytree 0.8, random_state 42-46;
         per user each model ranks candidates (rank 1 = best, ties -> candidate order), the mean rank is
         sorted ascending (ties -> candidate order). Compared with one model.
A change is kept only if the 95% CI of its MAP@5 A gain excludes 0 (exp 1 against v7; exp 2 against the
best configuration after exp 1, which is v7 when exp 1 is not kept).
v7_refinement.param_names_checked: subsample, subsample_freq, colsample_bytree, random_state in LGBMRanker.__init__ (lightgbm 4.7.0)
